clue.text: Disappointment with most of bulk arrests

indicators.note: arrests means holds or captures, so the shortened word holds the next piece inside it
most of says the word for bulk loses its final letter here

parts.note: bulk means size

explanation.surface: Someone is let down when most of a large consignment gets seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SIZE to SIZ, and 'arrests' puts W inside it. SWIZ is informal British slang for a swindle or a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A swiz is a British slang word for a swindle or something that turns out a letdown, hence a disappointment.

clue.text: Old fogey's maybe a hundred and one

definitions.meaning: a square is an old-fashioned conventional person, and fogey's reads as fogeys, the plural
100 and 1 are both perfect ..., ten squared and one squared

explanation.surface: Old fogeys come in a hundred and one varieties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hundred and one' looks like 'countless', but it names two numbers that are squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Square is slang for a conventional, unfashionable person, and 100 and 1 are perfect square numbers.

clue.text: Help to break ice, chiefly in case with bilateral agreement

indicators.note: to break means to split open, so the distress call goes inside the frozen water

parts.note: SOS is the distress call asking for help

indicators.note: chiefly means mostly, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: lest means in case

explanation.surface: An icebreaker offering help, mostly in a case where two sides agree.
explanation.walkthrough: SOS breaks ICE to make ISOSCE; 'chiefly' trims LEST to LES. 'ice-breaking' suggests a ship, but it is SOS going into ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, a playful 'bilateral agreement'.

clue.text: It jerks back seconds after swallowing one good portion

definitions.text: It jerks back seconds after swallowing one good portion

indicators.note: after places the seconds abbreviation at the end
swallowing means the reversed pair takes the following pieces inside it
back says the words It and jerks are read in reverse order and backwards

parts.note: taken as written
physical jerks are exercises, and PE is physical education
I is the Roman numeral for one
a lot is a portion or share

explanation.surface: A description of something snapping back a moment after a mouthful goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' is short for physical jerks, gym exercises. 'back' reverses the pair, 'swallowing' takes the next three pieces inside after its second letter, and 'after' puts S last. Read whole, the clue describes the flap that tips back when we swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the cartilage flap that folds back over the larynx when food is swallowed, so it jerks back after swallowing.

clue.text: Health practitioner picked up sparkling Evian water?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the answer is how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: sparkling water is fizzy; Evian is a French brand, and French for water is eau, said like the letter O

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist hears a request for some sparkling mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evian' signals French: water is eau, said like O. FIZZY-O is said like PHYSIO, British shorthand for a physiotherapist.
explanation.definitionFit: A physio is a physiotherapist, someone who treats injuries with exercise and massage.

clue.text: Grounded female boards assembled

indicators.note: boards means gets on, like boarding a ship, so the female goes inside

parts.note: gated means grounded, confined as a punishment
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A grounded woman climbs on board with the rest of the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounded' suggests aircraft, but GATED means kept in as a punishment; HER 'boards' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered means came together or collected, the same as assembled.

clue.text: Negotiable part cast where theatre's main action occurs

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A theatrical cast negotiating a part, centred on the main action of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors but rearranges NEGOTIABLE PART. 'theatre' is the operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hospital operating theatre the surgery happens on the operating table.

clue.text: Office worker on current rates for staff

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the current symbol follows

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A temp gets paid at going rates set for permanent staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi are the speeds of musical pieces, written above the stave of a score.

clue.text: Towering church hosting popular recordings of organ

indicators.note: towering means rising up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards, in reverse
hosting means having as a guest, so the church contains the next piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
in means popular or fashionable
LPs are long-playing records

explanation.surface: A tall church plays well-loved recordings of its organ music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' puts popular inside church, recordings follow, and 'Towering' reads the lot upwards in this down clue. 'organ' sounds musical; it is the spleen.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenic is the adjective relating to the spleen, a body organ.

clue.text: Luckily caught one hole in cash account

indicators.note: in places the caught, one and hole pieces inside the cash and account words

parts.note: coin means cash
a tally is an account or reckoning
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
I is the Roman numeral for one
a den is a hole or lair

explanation.surface: Someone was lucky to be caught with a hole in their cash accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the three short pieces between the cash and account words. A den as a 'hole' is an animal's lair.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincidentally means by chance, and something happening by happy chance happens luckily.

clue.text: Starting late, tribute of retired dons in visitors' study?

indicators.note: dons means puts on, like a garment, so the trimmed word wraps around the next piece
starting late means the word begins one letter later than usual, losing its first letter

parts.note: a eulogy is a spoken tribute

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word of is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A late-starting tribute to dons who have retired, sounding like a send-off for academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting late' trims EULOGY to ULOGY; 'retired' turns OF into FO, which ULOGY 'dons'. 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb. The visitors are those arriving in flying saucers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ufology is the study of unidentified flying objects, the supposed craft of alien visitors, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Current topic consuming Right and Left

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the topic word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: thema is a word for a theme or topic

explanation.surface: A political discussion whose subject takes in both the Right and the Left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts R inside THEMA, giving THERMA, then L follows. 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning topical; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air, used by gliders and soaring birds.

clue.text: City in legal position facing resistance in share review

indicators.note: in places the city, legal position and resistance pieces inside the word for share

parts.note: a ration is a share or allowance

indicators.note: facing means set up against, so resistance comes straight after the previous piece

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
onside is the legal position for a player in football
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A financial review of a stake held by a City firm, with talk of its legal standing and resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode is EC; onside is football's legal position. 'in#2' sets the run inside the share word after its first letter. 'share' looks like a stock but means a ration.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconsideration is a fresh look at a decision, which is what a review is.

clue.text: European-backed rifles recoiled after firing first shot

indicators.note: recoiled means sprang back, so the shortened word is read backwards
firing first means the opening letter is fired, or dismissed, from the word for guns

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, and backed says it supports the rifles from behind, so it goes at the end

explanation.surface: Guns kick back after the opening shot, in a picture of a European shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after firing first' drops the R; 'recoiled' reverses what is left, and 'European-backed' puts E at the back. 'shot' is a photograph, not a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photograph you take of yourself, and a photograph is commonly called a shot.

clue.text: Regular exercise city police department backed

parts.note: PE is physical education, or exercise
Rio de Janeiro is a city, commonly just Rio

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the department's letters are reversed

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A city police department runs a regular fitness programme for its officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns CID into DIC. CID is the British police's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something periodic recurs at fixed intervals, which makes it regular.

clue.text: Daughter may order mobile carrier in Saudi Arabia

indicators.note: mobile means movable, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A daughter might order a mobile phone network in Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile carrier' reads as a phone company, but 'mobile' shuffles MAY ORDER and the carrier is a camel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromedary is the one-humped Arabian camel, a beast of burden across Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Joke about the Bolognese — certainly not spicy food

indicators.note: about means around, so the joke word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a jape is a joke or prank
la is the Italian for 'the', as a person from Bologna would say
no means certainly not

explanation.surface: A joke about spaghetti Bolognese not being spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolognese' looks like the pasta sauce but means Italian, giving LA for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalapeno is a hot green chilli pepper, eaten as spicy food.

clue.text: Contents of travel-sick itinerant's gut

indicators.note: itinerant means wandering, so the letters wander into a new order
contents of means everything inside, so the outer letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: A wandering traveller with motion sickness empties the contents of their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' drops the outer letters of TRAVEL-SICK, leaving RAVELSIC, and 'itinerant's' rearranges those. 'gut' is the adjective, as in a gut reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A visceral feeling comes from deep inside rather than from reasoning, just as a gut instinct does.

clue.text: What remains of singlet and another used in alternation?

parts.note: a vest is a singlet, a sleeveless undershirt in British usage

indicators.note: used in alternation means only every other letter of it counts

parts.note: another means a second singlet, the same word again

explanation.surface: Wearing a singlet and swapping it for another one in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' repeats the word singlet, whose even letters give IGE. In Britain a vest is the undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace or remnant, what remains of something that has mostly gone.

clue.text: Slight indication son's leaving with asset of mine

indicators.note: is leaving says the son's letter departs from the word for indication

parts.note: a sign is an indication
ore is the valuable material taken from a mine

explanation.surface: A sign that a son has left the family business, taking his share of the mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 's leaving' is read as 'son is leaving'. 'Slight' is the verb, to snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub them, deliberately ignoring them.

clue.text: Passage of text remembering radical

indicators.note: Passage of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reading of a text recalls something radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views are far from the mainstream, which is what radical describes.

clue.text: Request a small fork in buffet

indicators.note: buffet means knocked about, so the fork's letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking for a small fork at a buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like the meal; it is the verb, to batter, rearranging FORK into KFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for something is to request it.

clue.text: Society went over books after issue not quite clear

indicators.note: after puts the society, went, over and books pieces after the issue piece; only society precedes it

parts.note: to emit is to issue
went means ran
spare means left over
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A society checks its accounts after an issue is not entirely clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells you EMIT comes earlier than its clue position. 'went over books' suggests auditing, but each word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Semitransparent means letting some light through, so only partly clear.

clue.text: Flash fight that's captured on camera

parts.note: mo is a moment, a flash
to vie is to fight or compete

explanation.surface: A sudden brawl recorded on someone's phone camera.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment: 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is a motion picture, filmed with a camera.

clue.text: Occupy home with five rodent traps

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: traps means catches inside, so the rodent holds the numeral

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A household rodent problem where five of the creatures get caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traps' puts V inside VOLE, making VOLVE. The trap picture misleads: the vole is the one doing the trapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve someone is to engage or occupy them in an activity.

clue.text: Trouble for one of interns overturning bags of leaves

indicators.note: overturning means turning upside down, so the assembled letters are read backwards
interns means confines, so the abbreviation for 'for one' and the word of enclose the trouble word

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one
taken as written
ail means to trouble

explanation.surface: Bothered interns tip over sacks of fallen leaves in an autumn chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interns' looks like trainees but is a verb: 'for one' plus 'of' confine the trouble word, and 'overturning' reverses the whole string, giving EGAILOF read backwards. 'bags of' is British for plenty of.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is the mass of leaves on a plant, so plenty of them, bags of leaves in informal British idiom.

clue.text: Panel on old comic strip that's abrasive

indicators.note: on means next to, so the panel word follows the comedian

parts.note: Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s
a board is a panel

explanation.surface: A panel discusses an old comic strip in a review of cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Emery was a popular British television comedian. 'comic strip' wants to go together, but 'strip' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emery board is a thin card coated with abrasive grit, used to file fingernails.

clue.text: Rely on playing stringed instrument

indicators.note: playing means fooling around, so the letters are fooled into a new order

explanation.surface: Depend on performing with a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges RELY; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient harp-like instrument with strings stretched on a frame.
